reason: The text contains multiple regular human characters with dialogue, emotions, and expressed opinions. Most prominently, Gideon is a regular Israelite who has extensive lines of speech, demonstrates emotions like fear and doubt ('O my Lord...why has all this befallen us?'), and expresses opinions questioning God's presence and his own ability to save Israel. Additionally, Gideon's father Joash speaks to defend him, the men of the city voice their demand for his death, and soldiers in the Midianite camp recount and interpret a dream. These are not merely narrated figures but active participants with direct discourse and emotional responses.
